acceptance: Throughput results expose whether work remains active, the affected stream/task identities, owned resources, and the last observable cleanup state.
A combined benchmark runner refuses to start maintenance or another measured phase and refuses to reuse or close affected shared resources while prior work is outstanding.
Timed-out or outstanding-work results omit invalid Throughput@Size and related metrics from public result artifacts rather than exporting a numeric sentinel as a valid measurement.
The normal healthy path and bounded timeout return remain bounded; no fix introduces an unbounded executor shutdown or join.

Tests use a controllable running query to prove the caller returns, the next phase is contained, queued work is cancelled, running work remains owned, and cleanup unblocks the boundary only after termination.
Adapters that support native query cancellation may use it, but unsupported adapters remain safe through containment and fail-closed status.
context: Containment comes before any universal cancellation abstraction. Cooperative events stop only between queries; already-running database calls require adapter-native cancellation or continued ownership until completion.
description:
StreamRunner intentionally returns without waiting for already-running threads because Python cannot forcibly cancel them. That bounded response is useful, but a timeout result does not expose enough ownership state for combined runners to prevent maintenance, later measured phases, teardown, or connection reuse while queries are still active. Add an explicit outstanding-work outcome and enforce containment at every phase boundary.

Decision boundary: preserve bounded timeout response. Do not add an unbounded join or claim that cooperative cancellation stops an in-flight database call. Prefer phase quarantine and resource ownership transfer until real termination is observed.
